json.reason: Classic JS API misuse: Array.prototype.sort() without a comparator sorts by string representation, which is wrong for numeric arrays; it is detectable syntactically as a zero-argument .sort() call.
json.title: Array.sort() called without a comparator function
json.message: .sort() without a comparator sorts elements as strings (e.g. [10, 9, 100] -> [10, 100, 9]); pass an explicit comparator.
json.note: Array.prototype.sort() converts elements to strings and compares them lexicographically by default, so numeric arrays end up in the wrong order. Pass a comparator such as (a, b) => a - b for numbers, or (a, b) => a.localeCompare(b) for strings, to make the ordering explicit and correct.
json.rule_yaml:
rule:
  kind: call_expression
  all:
    - pattern: $ARR.sort()
    - not:
        has:
          field: function
          has:
            field: property
            regex: "^(?!sort$)"
